newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila says ASEAN to discuss Burma membership.
newsitem.headline: Manila says ASEAN to discuss Burma membership.

text.p: The Philippines said on Saturday that the seven-nation ASEAN group would next month discuss plans to admit Burma as a member despite the opposition of the United States.

Foreign Secretary Domingo Siazon, reacting to a U.S. call on Friday for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations to drop plans to admit Rangoon, said it was "normal" for governments to lobby others to support their views.
Washington last week banned new American investment in Burma in fresh sanctions over the human rights record of its military rulers.

Commenting on the U.S. sanctions and opposition to Burma's entry to ASEAN, Siazon told reporters: "Normally, among countries, you lobby each other trying to convince them to adopt to your position. That's normal but of course we have taken note of their action."

Siazon added: "We will review our position because we have a meeting anyway on May 31 in Kuala Lumpur to determine and take a decision on the eventual membership of Cambodia, Laos and Myanmar (Burma)."
Foreign ministers of ASEAN, which comprises the Philippines, Malaysia, Indonesia, Singapore, Thailand, Brunei and Vietnam, are to attend the Kuala Lumpur meeting.
ASEAN ministers have said they have agreed the three countries should be admitted simultaneously but have not decided when.
Burma on Saturday urged ASEAN to "stick to its guns" and refuse to let Washington dictate to it.
